_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 8. Blau notes consulted: 8:1 ('God commanded a wind by which the water rested' — Saadia rewrites ויעבר as 'commanded'); 8:3, 8:5, 8:7 (hendiadys 'הלוך וX' → 'each time time passed, [it] X-ed' — Saadia's consistent pattern); 8:4 גבאל קרדא = 'mountains of Qardu' (Saadia identifies Ararat with Qardu/Kurdistan); 8:9 'all the face' (Saadia reads 'all' as modifying face, not land); 8:21 אלקרבאן אלמרצ'י = 'the pleasing offering' (rationalizes ריח ניחח), קאל אללה מן ד'אתה = 'God said from Himself' (rationalizes אל לבו).

translations.1: God remembered Noah, and all the wild creatures and the beasts who were with him in the ark; and God commanded a wind upon the earth, and by means of it the water grew still.
translations.2: And the springs of the deep were stopped up, and the windows of the sky; and the rain was withheld from the sky.
translations.3: And the water receded from upon the earth — each time time passed, it receded — and the water grew less after a hundred and fifty days.
translations.4: And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of it, upon the mountains of Qardu (Ararat).
translations.5: And the water — each time time passed, it grew less — until the tenth month; and on the first day of it, the heads of the mountains appeared.
translations.6: And when forty days had passed, Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made.
translations.7: And he sent forth the raven; and it kept going out and returning, until the water dried up from the face of the earth.
translations.8: Then he sent forth the dove from him, to see whether the water had abated from the face of the earth.
translations.9: But the dove did not find a resting-place for its foot, and it returned to him, to the ark, for the water was upon all the face of the earth. So he put out his hand and took it, and brought it in to him, into the ark.
translations.10: And he waited yet another seven days; and again he sent it forth from the ark.
translations.11: And it came to him at the time of evening; and behold, in its mouth was a plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the water had abated from the earth.
translations.12: And he waited yet another seven days; then he sent it forth — and it did not return to him again.
translations.13: And when it was in the year six hundred and one, on the first day of the first month, the water had dried up from upon the earth. And Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked — and behold, the face of the earth had dried.
translations.14: And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of it, the earth had dried out.
translations.15: And God spoke to Noah, saying:
translations.16: 'Go out from the ark — you and your wife, and your sons and your sons' wives with you.
translations.17: And all the wild creatures that are with you, of every corporeal being — of the bird, and of the beasts, and of every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth — bring them out with you, that they may breed in the earth, and bear fruit and multiply upon it.'
translations.18: And Noah went out, with his sons, and his wife and his sons' wives with him.
translations.19: And all the wild creatures and the creeping things and the bird, and the rest of what creeps upon the earth, according to their kinds — they went out from the ark.
translations.20: And Noah built an altar to God; and he took from some of the pure beasts and from some of the pure birds, and offered ascending offerings upon the altar.
translations.21: And God accepted the pleasing offering; and God said from Himself: 'I shall not again curse the earth on account of the human — even though the inclination of the human's heart is wicked from his youth — and I shall not again strike down every living thing as I have done.
translations.22: Always, throughout the lifetime of the earth — seedtime and harvest, the cold and the heat, the summer and the autumn, the day and the night — shall not cease.'
